title: Specialization and cospecialization commute with the fibre maps
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $G$ an abelian sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Suppose $f$ is locally acyclic relative to $G$ [def-weil-pbc-local-acyclicity-abelian-sheaf]. Fix a geometric point $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ [def-weil-geometric-point], put $S'=S_{(\bar s)}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and use the canonical lift of $\bar s$ over the closed point of $S'$ [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](1). Let $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega'\to S'$ be any geometric point. Set $X'=X\times_SS'$, $p:X'\to X$, $X_{\bar s}=X'\times_{S'}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, $X_{\bar t}=X'\times_{S'}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega'$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $i:X_{\bar s}\to X'$ and $h:X_{\bar t}\to X'$. Write $G'=p^{-1}G$ and $G_{\bar t}=h^{-1}G'$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], and place sheaves in degree zero in the bounded below derived categories of abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $\beta:G'[0]\to Rh_*(G_{\bar t}[0])$ be the unit of the derived adjunction $h^{-1}\dashv Rh_*$ [prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-adjunction], using derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and derived inverse image [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image]. Assume in addition that $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Derived global sections are those of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], and $R\Gamma(X',Rh_*G_{\bar t}[0])\cong R\Gamma(X_{\bar t},G_{\bar t}[0])$ is the canonical Leray identification [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-derived-unit](1). Define $cosp:R\Gamma(X_{\bar t},G_{\bar t}[0])\to R\Gamma(X_{\bar s},i^{-1}G'[0])$ by the inverse of this Leray identification, restriction along $i$, and $R\Gamma(X_{\bar s},(i^{-1}\beta)^{-1})$, where $i^{-1}\beta$ is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-local-acyclicity-closed-fibre-unit]. For $u=\bar s,\bar t$, let $\rho_u:(Rf_*G[0])_u\to R\Gamma(X_u,G|_{X_u}[0])$ be the canonical fibre map, namely the derived exchange [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] for the geometric-point cartesian square, followed by global sections over that geometric point [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk]. Derived stalks mean applying the exact geometric inverse image followed by exact global sections over the geometric point. Let $sp:(Rf_*G[0])_{\bar s}\to(Rf_*G[0])_{\bar t}$ be the map induced termwise by restricting pointed etale neighbourhood germs through $S'\to S$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]; the target point on $S$ is the composite of $\bar t$ with $S'\to S$. Then in $D^+(\operatorname{Ab})$,
$$cosp\circ\rho_{\bar t}\circ sp=\rho_{\bar s}.$$
No properness or torsion hypothesis is imposed, and no assertion that $sp$, $cosp$ or either $\rho_u$ is invertible is made.

proof.text: Apply the strict-local fibre-map factorization to obtain a comparison a whose specialization and closed-lift composites are the two derived restrictions.

Expand cospecialization as inverse Leray, restriction, and the inverse closed-fibre unit. Naturality of derived restriction moves the derived unit across restriction; the unit and its inverse cancel, leaving the closed-lift composite, which is the closed strict-base fibre map by the factorization.
